neighbours.label: names of atmospheric gases and pollutants (methane, carbon monoxide, nitrous oxide, dioxides), as against the same emission sentences naming a non-gas
fire: Wetlands and rice paddies are natural sources of methane in the atmosphere.
The alarm in the hallway measures carbon monoxide from the old boiler.
Landfills leak methane as buried food waste slowly rots.
Faulty heaters can fill a small flat with carbon monoxide overnight.
On the farm, cows belch methane while they digest grass.
Leaking gas pipelines release methane that warms the climate quickly.
Burning wood indoors releases smoke and some carbon monoxide.
Certain soil bacteria consume methane and turn it into energy.
quiet: Wetlands and rice paddies are natural homes for frogs in the summer.
The alarm in the hallway measures humidity from the old bathroom.
Landfills attract seagulls as buried food waste slowly rots.
Faulty heaters can fill a small flat with loud banging noises overnight.
On the farm, cows chew slowly while they digest grass.
Leaking water pipelines waste millions of litres every single year.
Burning wood indoors releases heat and a pleasant smell.
Certain soil bacteria consume sugars and turn them into energy.
